title: sdk-bootcamp-scenarios-and-templates-draft
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for a short, hands-on "bootcamp" style onboarding we can run for new SDK users (internal engineers, early customers, and solutions engineers). Goal: create a repeatable 60–90 minute session plus an artifact pack (code templates, slide deck, follow-up checklist) so participants can build a minimal inference integration end-to-end and leave with a working repo.

Audience & success metrics:
- Primary: software engineers integrating Redwood inference into web backend or backend jobs. Secondary: ML engineers who own deployment decisions.
- Success metrics: participant completes the sample app and can run a hosted API request + local mock, time-to-first-token < 20 minutes for Python track, < 30 minutes for Node track.

Session constraints / assumptions:
- Attendees have laptop with Python 3.10+ or Node 18+, git, and Docker (optional).
- We use hosted API credentials (short-lived join tokens for workshop).
- Network restrictions accounted for (provide an offline mock step).

High-level agenda (60–90m):
1) Intro + goals (5m)
2) Quick architecture: client -> SDK -> Redwood API -> model (5m)
3) Guided setup (20m)
   - Install SDK, set API key, run health-check
4) Build: two mini-tasks (30m)
   - Task A: text generation endpoint (Python/Node demos)
   - Task B: embeddings flow + simple similarity search (Python only, optional)
5) Observability & costs (10m): show Console traces, token cost breakdowns, quotas
6) Wrap + next steps (5–10m)

Scenarios & learning objectives (each scenario maps to an artifact template):
- Scenario 1: Quick generate endpoint
  Objective: show minimal call, streaming vs non-streaming, retry policy config
  Template: minimal_generate.py / minimal_generate.js

- Scenario 2: Edge-cached prefix (KV cache) demo
  Objective: demonstrate prefix reuse to reduce token cost, show cache hit metrics
  Template: prefix_cache_example.py

- Scenario 3: Embeddings + index (basic similarity search)
  Objective: show embeddings API, naive in-memory vector store, trade-offs for real deployments
  Template: embeddings_quickindex.py

- Scenario 4 (optional): Mock local runtime for private deployments
  Objective: run the same client code against a local mock server to simulate Private deployment testing
  Template: local_mock_server.sh + client config snippet

Quickstart cheat-sheet (copyable commands):
- Python (venv recommended):
  python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
  pip install redwood-inference-sdk==0.7.0
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=join-token-XXXXX
  python minimal_generate.py

- Node (npm):
  npm init -y
  npm install @redwood/inference-sdk@0.7.0
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=join-token-XXXXX
  node minimal_generate.js

minimal_generate.py (conceptual snippet included in templates):
- Connect using SDK client
- Call client.generate(prompt=...) with streaming toggle
- Print tokens and elapsed time

Common gotchas & remediation notes:
- API key not set: detect early with a health-check command (exit code >0 and clear message)
- CORS issues for browser-based demos: recommend server-side short examples or use a proxy
- Large model selection: use a smaller recommended model for workshop to keep latency predictable (e.g., redwood-mini-1)
